title: iTutorGroup automated age-screening settlement
system_purpose: Apply configured eligibility rules to online applications for remote tutoring roles
decision_impact: According to EEOC's complaint, configured software automatically rejected applications; the public source does not establish whether a human reviewed them before or after that action
affected_groups: Older U.S. tutor applicants;women aged 55 or older;men aged 60 or older;indirect students described by an EEOC spokesperson as losing an opportunity to learn from qualified tutors
verified_facts: EEOC announced a consent settlement. According to the EEOC complaint summarized in that announcement, iTutorGroup programmed application software with sex-specific age cutoffs and automatically rejected applicants; the announcement states U.S. tutor hiring had ceased.
reported_harm: EEOC alleged discriminatory loss of employment opportunity and obtained monetary and non-monetary relief; settlement does not itself adjudicate liability, establish the human workflow, or prove an AI model caused the conduct.
quantitative_evidence: EEOC reported more than 200 qualified U.S. applicants rejected during the relevant conduct and $365,000 in settlement relief; the public announcement does not provide the total applicant denominator.
limitations: EEOC-hosted testimony explicitly says the mechanism may have been rule-based automation rather than AI. No source code, model audit, full applicant denominator, human-review record, or causal technical analysis is public.

title: Amazon experimental recruiting model abandoned after internal bias signal
system_purpose: Score and rank technical-role resumes to help recruiters locate promising applications
decision_impact: Lower scores could reduce recruiter attention, although sources do not show sole model control of a final decision
affected_groups: Women applicants;graduates of women's colleges;technical-role applicants;recruiters
verified_facts: Reuters reported that Amazon began the experimental project in 2014, identified non-neutral gender behavior by 2015, attempted targeted edits, and later abandoned the project; EEOC-hosted testimony repeats the account as a cautionary example.
reported_harm: The sources report that women-associated terms and two women's colleges could lower scores, creating a foreseeable discriminatory opportunity-loss hazard; they do not document a regulator finding or a confirmed harmed applicant.
quantitative_evidence: The reported model learned from resumes submitted over a ten-year period and produced scores from one to five stars; no evaluation denominator, subgroup rate, production-decision count, or harmed-applicant count was reported.
limitations: The central evidence is secondary reporting based on unnamed sources. It was an experimental tool, recruiters reportedly did not rely solely on it, and the available evidence does not prove realized discriminatory hiring outcomes.

title: Mobley v. Workday litigation—conditionally certified ADEA collective; merits unresolved as of August 2026
system_purpose: Alleged and court-defined scope for preliminary certification: applications scored, sorted, ranked, or screened by enabled Workday AI features; Workday disputes plaintiffs' characterization of the functions and effects
decision_impact: An alleged denial of employment recommendation could withhold or deprioritize an application before employer consideration
affected_groups: Applicants aged 40 or older;Black applicants;applicants with disabilities;employer customers
verified_facts: EEOC filed an amicus brief on legal coverage while expressly taking no position on factual accuracy. In May 2025 the court provisionally certified an age-discrimination collective for notice purposes. A 28 July 2026 discovery order shows the litigation remained active and addressed access to customer applicant data, not whether discrimination occurred.
reported_harm: Plaintiffs allege disparate employment opportunity based on age, race, and disability; Workday disputes the allegations, and none of the cited orders found discrimination, disparate impact, or technical causation on the merits.
quantitative_evidence: The complaint account in the EEOC brief says the named plaintiff applied to more than 100 positions beginning in 2017 and was rejected each time; the provisionally certified collective covers applicants aged 40 or older from the court-defined period, but no final class count or causal rate is established.
limitations: Conditional certification, pleadings, and discovery orders are not merits findings. The latest cited official order is 28 July 2026; employer configuration varies, and public evidence does not establish a common model effect, denominator, damages, or causal mechanism.
